 Belated ITR Filing Deadline December 31: Can taxpayers still claim refunds and carry forward losses?
 Written By Bhawna Gupta Published: 5:27 PM, Nov 20, 2026 | Updated: 5:28 PM, Nov 20, 2026 A belated return is an income tax return filed after the original due date. Under Section 139(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, taxpayers who missed their filing deadline can submit their returns within the prescribed extended period. Taxpayers can claim eligible income tax refunds even when they file a belated return. ChatGPT generated/Representative Image Missing the income tax return (ITR) filing deadline does not mean taxpayers have lost their chance to submit their returns. The Income Tax Department allows people who missed the original deadline to file a belated return. For Assessment Year (AY) 2026-27, the last date to file a belated ITR is December 31, 2026, or before the completion of assessment, whichever is earlier.
 However, filing late comes with certain disadvantages. While taxpayers can still claim eligible income tax refunds, they may lose the benefit of carrying forward some losses to future years.
 Here is what taxpayers should know before filing a belated return.
 What is a belated ITR? 
 A belated return is an income tax return filed after the original due date. Under Section 139(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, taxpayers who missed their filing deadline can submit their returns within the prescribed extended period.
 For example, if a salaried employee failed to file an ITR within the applicable due date, they can still complete the process before December 31, 2026.
 The deadline applies to returns for income earned during the financial year 2025-26.
 Can you still claim an income tax refund? 
 Yes, taxpayers can claim eligible income tax refunds even when they file a belated return.
 Suppose an employee's employer deducted Rs 60,000 as TDS during the financial year, but the employee's final income tax liability comes to Rs 40,000.
 In this case, the employee may be eligible for a refund of Rs 20,000.
 Even if the employee files the return after the original deadline, the refund can still be claimed through a belated ITR.
 However, late filing may affect the interest received on the refund. In applicable cases, refund interest is calculated from the date of filing rather than from the beginning of the assessment year.
 The refund will be issued after the Income Tax Department processes the return and verifies the claim.
 Can taxpayers carry forward losses? 
 This is where filing a return late can create problems. Under income tax rules, certain losses can be carried forward to future financial years only when the return is filed within the original due date.
 For example, suppose an investor suffered a capital loss of Rs 1 lakh from selling shares during FY2025-26.
 If the investor did not file the return within the prescribed deadline, the loss generally cannot be carried forward to adjust against eligible capital gains in future years.
 Similar restrictions apply to business losses and certain other losses, including losses from futures and options trading.
 However, there is an important exception. Losses under the head 'Income from House Property' can generally be carried forward even if the return is filed late, subject to the applicable rules.
 Therefore, taxpayers should understand the type of loss before assuming that it can be carried forward.
 What are the penalties for late filing? 
 Filing a belated return may also attract a late filing fee under Section 234F.
 For taxpayers whose total income exceeds Rs 5 lakh, the fee can be Rs 5,000.
 For those whose total income does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, the fee is limited to Rs 1,000.
 Interest may also apply if the taxpayer has outstanding income tax that was not paid within the prescribed time.
 For example, someone who has already paid all their taxes through TDS may not have additional tax to pay, but a late filing fee could still apply depending on their income and filing requirements.
